newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corp debt issuance to pick up as yields drop.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corp debt issuance to pick up as yields drop.

text.p: Corporate bond new issue activity is expected to pick up once more amid an improved rate environment following Friday's stormy trading session in the U.S. Treasury market, dealers said.
"The government market is in better shape then it was when we left on Friday," said one syndicate source. "It's getting down to the wire...only a few weeks are left so deals should get done now."
Among the deals expected to come this week are Deutsche Bank's $1.0 billion in Aa1/AA-plus rated 10-year yankee debt via lead manager Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
Also, Crown Cork & Seal Inc is expected to issue $1.2 billion in a multi-tranche debt offering as early as this week via Salomon Brothers Inc, sources added.
Proceeds from the offering will be used to refinance a portion of the $1.9 billion of indebtedness arising from the February 1996 acquisition of CarnaudMetalbox S.A., the company said.
In addition, Nike Inc is getting set to come to market with a $150 million seven-year debt offering via lead manager Goldman Sachs & Co.

Corporate debt offerings are expected to flow in during the next two weeks as issuers wrap up their financing needs ahead of the holidays and investors stand ready to scoop up the paper, dealers said.
"There's still very good demand for corporate paper," said another syndicate source. "The rate environment is very good right now so we'll probably see a lot of paper in the next two weeks."
Last week, the corporate bond primary market saw about $3.0 billion in new straight debt priced, dealers said.
Among other issues, Rite Aid is expected to tap the market with a three-tranche deal via Goldman Sachs & Co late this week to early next week, syndicate sources said.
The deal is expected to be rated A3/BBB-plus and consist of a $200 million five-year isssue, $200 million in a 10-year issue and $200 million in a 30-year issue, they added.
Capital One Financial Corp is expected to set $125 million in seven-year debt via Donaldson Lufkin and Jenrette Securities.
Union Central Life is still expected to bring a $500 million two-part debt offering near-term, sources said.
AES China Generating Co is expected to issue $180 million in a 10-year senior note offering via Morgan Stanley. Initial talk on the size of the deal was $150 million, dealers said.
Turning to the high-yield arena, another $1.6 billion in corporate debt is expected to hit the market this week, dealers added.
Among the issuers are AK Steel Corp's $550 million in Ba2/BB-minus 10-year 144A senior notes via CS First Boston, dealers said.
Phonetel Tech is also expected to issue $110 million in senior notes due 2006 via JP Morgan Securities.
Jacor Communications is expected to issue $125 million in 10-year senior subordinated notes via Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette.
Quest Diagnostics is expected to issue $150 million in senior subordinated notes due 2006 via JP Morgan Securities.
Delta Beverage Group is also expected to issue $120 million in seven-year 144A notes via NationsBanc.
Plastic Containers Inc is expected to issue $115 million in 10-year 144A notes via Donaldson Lufkin and Jenrette.
Scholastic Brands is expected to set $90 million in seven-year 144A senior subordinated notes via Lehman Brothers. Price talk on the issue is between 11.0 and 11.25 percent.
Veitas Holdings is expected to issue $135 million in seven-year 144A notes via Donaldson Lufkin and Jenrette.
Katz Media Corp is expected to set $100 million in 10-year 144A notes via DLJ as well.
Safelite Glass Corp is also expected to tap the market with $100 million in 10-year 144A senior subordinated notes via Chase Securities.
In the government market, the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond is up 15/32 at 100-10/32 to yield 6.48 percent.
